subject: Human Evolution
title: Did They Speak?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Did They Speak? usable.

hook.text: Neanderthals had the FOXP2 gene—the same variant linked to speech and language in modern humans.

buildup.text: Their hyoid bone—key to controlling the tongue during speech—is virtually identical to ours.

discovery.text: Inner ear structures suggest they could hear the same sound frequencies we use for spoken language.

twist.text: Having the hardware doesn't prove complex language. Their smaller cerebellum may have limited syntax.

climax.text: Most researchers now agree Neanderthals had some form of spoken communication—the debate is how complex.

punchline.text: They could talk. We're still debating what.

quiz.question: What evidence suggests Neanderthals could speak?
options: FOXP2 gene, hyoid bone, and ear structures matching modern humans
